title: Revelation, Chapter Four Part II
summary: William Branham continues his series on Revelation chapter 4, discussing the voice of the trumpet, the throne in heaven, and the living creatures. He emphasizes trusting God's promises, using examples from Abraham, Noah, and John the Baptist, and contrasts worldly wisdom with God's wisdom.
themes: Contrast between worldly and divine wisdom

title: Questions and Answers
summary: William Branham addresses a group of ministers, deacons, and trustees, answering questions about calling to ministry, speaking in tongues, and the fruit of the Spirit. He emphasizes that the evidence of the Holy Ghost is a Christ-like life, not tongues, and that God's call must be confirmed in one's heart.
themes: Fruit of the Spirit vs. gifts

title: The Messiah
summary: William Branham preaches on the meaning of 'Messiah' as the Anointed One and King, emphasizing that Jesus fulfilled all prophecies. He explains that believers, as 'Messiahettes,' are anointed with the same Spirit to perform signs and wonders, and calls the church to return to the Word and the power of the Holy Spirit.

title: Things That Wasn't So From The Beginning
subtitle: 61-0119M
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of returning to the original Word of God, emphasizing that truth is found at the beginning. He criticizes denominations for perverting God's Word with creeds and traditions, and calls for a return to the Pentecostal experience and the power of the Holy Spirit as seen in the early church.

title: Queen of Sheba
summary: William Branham preaches on the Queen of Sheba's journey to hear Solomon's wisdom as a type of the end-time generation seeking the sign of the resurrection. He contrasts the faith of those who hunger for God with the unbelief of a wicked and adulterous generation, emphasizing that the same Gospel that blinded the Jews now blinds the Gentiles, while the true Church rallies around the gift of the Holy Spirit.

title: The Water Baptism
summary: William Branham uses the analogy of a rifle that must be perfectly zeroed to discuss the apparent contradiction between Matthew 28:19 (baptizing in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost) and Acts 2:38 (baptizing in the name of Jesus Christ). He argues that the Bible must be perfectly consistent and that the solution lies in understanding that Father, Son, and Holy Ghost are titles, not names, and that the one Name is Jesus. He emphasizes that spiritual revelation, not seminary teaching, is the key to understanding Scripture.

title: Mary's Belief
summary: William Branham preaches on Mary's encounter with the angel Gabriel, emphasizing her faith in God's Word despite the impossibility of a virgin birth. He draws parallels to the present day, urging believers to accept God's promises without requiring signs, and highlights the role of the Holy Spirit as God's messenger in the last days.

title: As The Eagle Stirs Her Nest
summary: William Branham uses the metaphor of an eagle to describe the Christian life, emphasizing the need to rise above worldly creeds and distractions through faith in God. He shares personal experiences observing eagles in nature, drawing parallels to spiritual truths about God's protection, the power of the Holy Spirit, and the importance of living a high and holy life. The sermon encourages believers to trust in God's provision and to soar above the limitations of denominationalism.
themes: Eagle as symbol of the believer

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, drawing parallels between physical blindness and spiritual blindness. He emphasizes the importance of faith, holding onto God's promises, and the need for love and compassion in the church.
themes: The Holy Spirit as God's representative

title: Why?
summary: William Branham preaches on the question 'Why?' from Jeremiah 8:22, asking why God's people are not recovered when there is balm in Gilead and a Physician. He uses the story of King Ahaziah and Elijah to illustrate that people reject God's remedy due to stubbornness and selfishness. Branham emphasizes the need for genuine new birth and the Holy Spirit, warning against substitutes and compromise.
themes: the power of the Holy Spirit

title: Expectation
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of expectation based on faith in God's promises, using examples from Abraham, Moses, and Simeon. He encourages believers to separate from unbelief and expect God to fulfill His Word, especially regarding healing and the Holy Spirit.

title: Expectation
summary: William Branham opens a revival series in Long Beach, emphasizing the need for genuine revival through prayer and full obedience to God. He uses biblical examples like Noah, Abraham, and Moses to illustrate the power of expectation based on God's Word, and encourages the congregation to prepare their hearts for healing and spiritual renewal.

title: JEHOVAH-JIREH
summary: William Branham preaches on the covenant God made with Abraham, emphasizing that it was unconditional and based on grace, not law. He contrasts Abraham's faith with the lukewarm state of the modern church, urging believers to separate from the world and fully trust God's promises.

title: Abraham's Covenant Confirmed
summary: William Branham continues his study in Genesis, focusing on Abraham's covenant with God. He contrasts the faith of Abraham with the lukewarm Laodicean church age, emphasizing the need for separation from the world and a return to original Pentecostal faith. He also discusses the coming of Elijah and the restoration of the church.

title: Abraham
summary: William Branham continues his series on Abraham, discussing the patriarch's faith and obedience to God. He emphasizes the importance of staying true to God's promises and warns against the dangers of worldliness and organization in the church. The sermon includes testimonies of healing and missionary work.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham shares personal anecdotes and teachings on faith, the Holy Spirit, and the story of Abraham offering Isaac. He emphasizes trusting God's provision and the importance of being led by the Spirit.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit

title: And Thy Seed Shall Possess the Gate of His Enemies
summary: William Branham preaches on the promise to Abraham that his seed would possess the gate of his enemies, emphasizing that believers are Abraham's seed through Christ and must endure trials to receive the promise. He illustrates this with the story of the three Hebrew children in the fiery furnace and encourages steadfast faith.

title: The Basis of Fellowship
summary: William Branham speaks on the true basis of fellowship with God and one another, emphasizing that human efforts such as education, denominations, and science cannot restore fellowship. He stresses that only through the Blood of Jesus Christ can fellowship be achieved, using examples from the Bible and his own ministry experiences.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit

title: The Mark Of The Beast And The Seal Of God
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical concepts of the Mark of the Beast and the Seal of God, tracing their origins from Genesis through Revelation. He argues that the Seal of God is the baptism of the Holy Ghost, while the mark of the beast is the rejection of it, and emphasizes that these two forces are at work in the world today.

title: The Mark of the Beast and the Seal of God 2
summary: William Branham continues his teaching on the Mark of the Beast and the Seal of God, emphasizing that the Seal of God is the Holy Spirit and the mark of the beast is rejection of the Holy Spirit. He traces this conflict from Cain and Abel through history, warning that in the last days, only those sealed with the Holy Spirit will escape God's judgment.

title: The Queen of Sheba
summary: William Branham preaches on the Queen of Sheba's visit to Solomon as a type of the church seeking Christ. He contrasts the wisdom of Solomon with the greater wisdom of Christ, emphasizing that true faith comes by revelation and that the same signs and wonders that followed Christ should follow believers today.

title: Be Not Afraid
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of fear versus faith, using the biblical account of Jesus walking on water and the disciples' testimony meeting in the boat. He emphasizes that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that the sign of the Messiah—discerning the thoughts of the heart—is still active today. Branham encourages the congregation to have faith and not be afraid, as God's presence is with them.

title: Beyond The Curtain Of Time
summary: William Branham shares a vision of the afterlife given to him by God, describing a place of perfect love, youth, and joy beyond the curtain of time. He encourages believers to press on in faith, love, and obedience to the Word, and to embrace divine healing through genuine faith in Christ's sacrifice.

title: Expectations
summary: William Branham opens a revival meeting in Virginia, explaining his approach to divine healing and the importance of faith in God's Word. He emphasizes that healing was accomplished at Calvary and must be accepted by faith, not feelings. He also outlines the logistics of prayer cards and the meeting schedule.

title: An Uncertain Sound
summary: William Branham preaches on the uncertainty of the times, including national security, jobs, home life, politics, and the church. He emphasizes that only God's Word is certain and calls for a return to the true gospel and the experience of the Holy Ghost.
themes: the certain sound of the gospel

title: The Church Choosing Law For Grace
summary: William Branham preaches on the parallel between Israel's mistake of choosing law over grace and the Pentecostal church's similar error of organizing and adding works to grace. He warns that unbelief and reliance on human systems keep believers from entering the full promise of God.

title: Abraham's Grace Covenant
summary: William Branham preaches on the covenant God made with Abraham, emphasizing that it was a covenant of grace, not law, and that believers become Abraham's seed through the Holy Spirit. He contrasts faith with unbelief, warning against turning away from revealed truth, and applies the covenant to divine healing and the believer's security in Christ.

title: Abraham's Covenant Confirmed
summary: William Branham continues his series on Abraham, showing how God's covenant with Abraham and the signs given to him are mirrored in the Church age. He emphasizes that the last sign given to Abraham—the Angel revealing the thoughts of Sarah—is the same sign being manifested in the Church today, preceding the change of the body and the rapture.

title: Jezebel Religion
summary: William Branham preaches on the parallels between ancient Israel under Ahab and Jezebel and modern America, warning against spiritual decline, compromise with worldly systems, and the rise of a Jezebel-like religious spirit. He calls for a return to the pure Word of God and the power of the Holy Spirit.
themes: Return to the Word of God

title: The True Easter Seal
summary: William Branham delivers an Easter sermon on the true meaning of the Easter seal, contrasting it with worldly seals and offerings. He traces the conflict between Cain and Abel through history, showing how greed and rejection of God's provided way lead to persecution of the righteous. He emphasizes that Christ's resurrection is the ultimate seal of victory over sin and death, and calls for clean-cut decisions for God.

title: SIRS, WE WOULD SEE JESUS
summary: William Branham opens a revival campaign in Bloomington, Illinois, emphasizing that divine healing and salvation are based on faith in the finished work of Christ at Calvary. He argues that God is infinite and unchanging, and that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, therefore the same signs and wonders should be seen today. Using the account of the Greeks who said 'Sirs, we would see Jesus,' he challenges believers to seek a living encounter with the risen Christ rather than mere historical knowledge.
themes: divine healing as part of the Gospel
the role of the Holy Spirit
the need for personal encounter with Jesus

title: Conferences
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of conferences, drawing parallels between worldly conferences and divine conferences with God. He emphasizes the need for the church to come together, lay aside differences, and be inspired by the Holy Spirit, using the example of an eagle's faith and confidence in its wings to illustrate trusting in God's power.
themes: The eagle as a symbol of faith

title: A Greater Than Solomon Is Here
summary: William Branham speaks on the greatness of Christ compared to Solomon, using the Queen of Sheba's visit as a type. He shares testimonies of healing and revival in Africa, emphasizing that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that His works vindicate His Word.

title: Why?
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of faith in God's Word for healing, explaining the nature of his prophetic gift and the role of the believer's faith. He addresses why many are not healed despite God's provision, using biblical examples and personal testimonies to encourage trust in God's promises.

title: Be Not Afraid, It Is I
summary: William Branham preaches on faith and divine healing, emphasizing that healing was accomplished at Calvary and is received by faith. He uses the biblical account of Jesus walking on water and the testimonies of the disciples to illustrate that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that His presence is manifested through spiritual gifts.

title: From That Time
summary: William Branham shares personal anecdotes and a sermon on the transformative power of encountering God. He emphasizes that true change comes from a divine encounter, not external reforms, and calls for unity and love among believers.

title: The Uncertain Sound
summary: William Branham preaches on the uncertainty of the world—in national security, jobs, politics, and the church—contrasting it with the certainty of God's Word. He shares a personal vision of Christ's intercession and urges believers to trust in the unchanging Word of God.

title: Abraham And His Seed After Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the Abrahamic covenant, emphasizing that God's promises to Abraham and his seed are unconditional and based on election. He calls believers to total separation from the world, warning that compromise hinders revival.

title: Abraham And His Seed After Him
summary: William Branham preaches on Galatians 3:29, explaining that believers in Christ are Abraham's seed and heirs according to the promise. He traces the parallels between God's dealings with Abraham and the Church, emphasizing election, grace, justification, sanctification, and the confirmation of the covenant through Christ's sacrifice.

title: The Greatest News Flash in History
summary: William Branham preaches on the resurrection of Jesus Christ as the greatest news flash in history, emphasizing that Christ appears only to His elected believers and that the church must move beyond dead creeds and organizations to experience the living Christ. He calls believers to 'come, see, and go tell' the message of the resurrected Lord.

title: The Godhead Explained
summary: William Branham addresses a gathering of ministers in Chicago, explaining his stance on the Godhead and the divisions among Pentecostal groups over water baptism and the Trinity. He advocates for unity and love among believers, emphasizing that both the Oneness and Trinitarian positions are wrong when they argue, and that the true focus should be on winning souls to Christ.

title: The Forgotten Beatitude
summary: William Branham preaches on Matthew 11:6, 'Blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me,' calling it the forgotten beatitude. He uses the example of John the Baptist, who became discouraged in prison and doubted Jesus, to encourage believers not to be offended when God's ways don't match their expectations. Branham emphasizes that God is always on schedule and that the same works Jesus did are being repeated in the evening time.

title: Micaiah The Prophet
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Micaiah the prophet from 1 Kings 22, emphasizing the importance of speaking only what God says regardless of popular opinion. He contrasts true prophets with those who compromise, and encourages believers to stay faithful to God's Word.

title: Only Believe
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of faith, using the story of Jairus from Luke 8:50. He encourages believers to confess their faith openly, even when facing opposition, and emphasizes that God's power is available to meet every need.

title: Getting In The Spirit
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for the Church to return to the Holy Spirit, using the story of Elisha and the minstrel from 2 Kings 3:15. He laments that the Church has become dry and fruitless through organization and division, and calls for a revival of love, unity, and the genuine power of God.

title: One Of The Meanest Men In Town
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Simon the Pharisee and the sinful woman who anointed Jesus' feet. He contrasts the cold, self-righteous welcome of the religious leader with the humble, tearful devotion of the outcast, urging listeners to truly welcome Jesus and not leave Him with 'dirty feet.'

title: The Uncertain Sound
summary: William Branham preaches on the uncertainty of the world—nations, jobs, homes, politics, and churches—contrasting it with the certainty of God's Word. He uses biblical examples like Noah, Moses, Elijah, and David to illustrate unwavering faith in God's promises, encouraging believers to trust God's Word despite worldly instability.

title: Super Sign
summary: William Branham preaches on the 'Super Sign' promised by God in Isaiah 7:14—a virgin conceiving and bearing a Son, Immanuel. He contrasts man's failed attempts at super achievements (towers, cities, ships, organizations) with God's eternal supernatural sign: God made flesh among His people. Branham emphasizes that the same supernatural signs of Christ's resurrection are available today through a supernatural people born of Abraham's faith.

title: A Greater Than Solomon Is Here
summary: William Branham speaks about the power of prayer, the gifts of the Spirit, and the importance of faith. He shares testimonies of healings and recounts his missionary experiences in Africa, emphasizing that true Christianity is demonstrated through the power of God, not just theology.

title: God's Provided Way
subtitle: 61-0516M
summary: William Branham speaks on God's provided way for salvation and healing, contrasting man's failed attempts at achievement through science and human effort with God's perfect provision in Jesus Christ. He emphasizes that faith in God's Word and acceptance of Christ's finished work at Calvary is the only way to receive God's blessings.

title: Jesus Christ The Same Yesterday, Today, And Forever
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He argues that divine healing and salvation are already accomplished through Christ's sacrifice, and that faith in God's Word is essential to receive these blessings. Branham uses the example of Nathanael's encounter with Jesus to illustrate how Christ reveals Himself as Messiah through supernatural knowledge.
themes: the Messianic sign of a prophet

title: IT IS I
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of simple childlike faith and the power of prayer. He recounts the testimonies of the apostles, emphasizing that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that His presence is with believers today.
themes: Jesus as the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: SIRS, WE WOULD SEE JESUS
summary: William Branham speaks on the desire to see Jesus, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He discusses the role of divine healing as a sign of Christ's presence and the importance of faith over education or tradition in recognizing Him.

title: From That Time
summary: William Branham speaks on the phrase 'from that time,' illustrating how pivotal moments—whether sinful or redemptive—change a person's life. He shares personal anecdotes and biblical examples, emphasizing that meeting God transforms a person forever.

title: Show Us The Father
summary: William Branham speaks on the human cry to see God, using the account of Philip in John 14:8. He explores four ways to see God: in His universe, in His Word, in His Son, and in His people. He emphasizes that God is present and can be seen through nature, faith, and the indwelling Holy Spirit.

title: Revelation, Chapter Five Part I
summary: William Branham announces his departure from the ministry due to some followers falsely claiming he is the Messiah, which he denounces as a lie of the devil. He then continues his sermon series on Revelation, focusing on the seven-sealed book and the mercy seat guarded by the four living creatures, emphasizing the earnest of the Holy Spirit as the seal of believers' adoption.

title: Revelation, Chapter Five Part II
summary: William Branham discusses recent events, including a fulfilled vision and a doctrinal controversy that was resolved. He emphasizes staying true to the Word of God, warns against false spiritual gifts, and introduces the theme of redemption through the Lamb as a Kinsman Redeemer, using the story of Ruth and Boaz as an illustration.

title: The Ever-Present Water From The Rock
summary: William Branham shares a personal dream and his struggle with God's leading regarding his ministry location. He then teaches from Exodus 17, using the rock struck by Moses as a type of Christ, emphasizing that the Holy Spirit (the water) follows believers continually, just as the rock followed Israel.

title: God Being Misunderstood
summary: William Branham addresses questions from the congregation on topics including baptism, the Godhead, tithing, spiritual gifts, and biblical prophecy. He emphasizes the importance of reverence in church, correct baptismal formula, and discerning the Holy Spirit's work without judging individuals.

title: The Sixfold Purpose of Gabriel's Visit to Daniel
summary: William Branham continues his series on Daniel, focusing on the sixfold purpose of Gabriel's visit to Daniel as recorded in Daniel 9:24. He explains each purpose: to finish transgression, make an end of sins, make reconciliation for iniquity, bring in everlasting righteousness, seal up vision and prophecy, and anoint the Most Holy. Branham connects these purposes to the future restoration of Israel and the second coming of Christ.

title: The Seventieth Week of Daniel
summary: William Branham explains the prophecy of Daniel's seventy weeks, demonstrating how it applies to the Jewish people and reveals the timeline of the Messiah's coming. He emphasizes that the Jews are God's timepiece and that the Church age is separate from the prophetic weeks. Branham concludes that the prophecy precisely points to Jesus Christ as the Messiah.

title: Thy House
summary: William Branham speaks on the promise that believing on the Lord Jesus Christ brings salvation to one's household, using the examples of the Philippian jailer and Job. He encourages faith for family members and emphasizes that God honors the faith of parents for their children.

title: Faith
summary: William Branham teaches that the power of God resides within every believer through the Holy Spirit, and that faith is the law that activates that power for salvation, healing, and all needs. He uses the examples of Jesus' resurrection, Abraham's faith, and the Philippian jailer to illustrate that faith in God's promises brings forth what is already within. He also addresses a Catholic convert and warns against organizational formalism.

title: The Message of Grace
summary: William Branham shares a personal experience of seeing three rainbows in a field, confirming his message that Jesus is Jehovah of the Old Testament. He then preaches on grace, using Zechariah 4 to emphasize that salvation is not by might or power but by God's Spirit, and that grace has been God's plan from Eden onward.

title: Let Your Light So Shine Before Men
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of Christians being living examples of Christ, using the metaphor of a billboard to illustrate how believers should attract others to God through their actions. He emphasizes that the world sees Christ through believers, and that a genuine Christian life will make others hunger for righteousness.

title: The Comforter
summary: William Branham speaks on the Holy Spirit as the Comforter, emphasizing that the Word of God is our comfort and heritage. He draws examples from Noah, Job, and Abraham to illustrate unwavering faith in God's promises, even in times of trial and suffering.

title: Questions and Answers
summary: William Branham answers questions from the congregation on topics including water baptism in Jesus' name, the interpretation of Hebrews 6:4-6 and 10:26-39, the meaning of Jesus' command to 'feed my sheep,' and whether being slain in the Spirit is a sign of a husband's salvation. He emphasizes the importance of following Scripture and warns against rejecting further light from God.
themes: the promised land as type of Holy Spirit baptism

title: Respects
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of giving respect and reverence to God and His messengers. He uses biblical examples such as Noah, Moses, and Elijah to illustrate how God demands respect and how disrespect leads to judgment. He encourages believers to honor God's Word and His anointed servants.
themes: Fear of God as beginning of wisdom
God's mercy and way of escape
Vindication of God's servants through signs

title: The Testimony of a True Witness
summary: William Branham shares his gratitude for the congregation's support during his mother's illness and death, describing a vision where he saw her restored to youth. He emphasizes the certainty of the Christian faith through the testimony of nature, Scripture, and personal experience, urging believers to be true witnesses of Christ's resurrection.

title: Perfect Strength By Perfect Weakness
summary: William Branham preaches on the paradox that God's strength is made perfect in human weakness, using Paul's testimony in 2 Corinthians 12:9 as the text. He emphasizes that believers must surrender their own abilities, education, and strengths to become vessels God can use, drawing examples from biblical heroes like Paul and the apostles.
themes: human weakness as a prerequisite for divine strength
surrender of self and abilities to God
God's choice of the weak and rejected
dependence on God rather than human wisdom or education
the danger of relying on denominational strength
the need for a 'killing' of self before revival
